mainTopic: Rice and the מזונות ברכה: the refutation of רב ושמואל, and the ברכות before and after grains, rice, and the שבעת המינים
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining why רב ושמואל needed two statements. 'כל שיש בו' teaches that mixtures with the five grains get בורא מיני מזונות. 'כל שהוא' teaches that only the five grains get it, so אורז and דוחן do not, even when eaten plain. The גמרא defends this against two ברייתות: rice bread is only partly 'like a מעשה קדרה', and the ברייתא that lists rice as a real מעשה קדרה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי, who holds that rice is a true grain. A תוספתא then gives cooked rice בורא מיני מזונות. It cannot follow רבי יוחנן בן נורי, so it must follow the רבנן, and רב ושמואל are refuted (תיובתא). The גמרא then examines that תוספתא line by line. Chewed wheat gets בורא פרי האדמה according to the רבנן but בורא מיני זרעים according to רבי יהודה. Whether rice gets מעין שלש afterward depends on a dispute between רבן גמליאל and the חכמים, illustrated by the story in יריחו where רבי עקיבא followed the majority. A new version of the dispute, quoted by רבי יהודה, begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the second statement was needed: mixtures count too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its first answer: the statement 'כל שיש בו' teaches that a mixture containing the five grains also gets בורא מיני מזונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the statement 'anything that HAS [the five grains] in it' comes to teach us that.
steps.whatsHappening: This line wraps up an answer that started on the previous amud. It explains why רב ושמואל needed their second statement, 'כל שיש בו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the גמרא said: if we only had 'כל שהוא', we might think only pure grain gets מזונות, and a mixture does not. So 'כל שיש בו' teaches that even a mixture of the five grains with other foods gets מזונות. This closes the first half of the 'why do we need both?' answer.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes to teach us (introduces the point a statement is making)
Anything that has in it (i.e., a mixture that contains grain)

phrases.english: He teaches us: 'anything that has [of the five grains] in it.'
phrases.notes: End of an answer that began on the previous part of the daf.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן — כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun on the previous amud, explaining the need for רב ושמואל's 'כל שיש בו' statement.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'כל שיש בו' is needed to include grain mixtures in בורא מיני מזונות.

steps.title: Why the first statement was needed: what we might have wrongly thought
steps.stepSummary: If we only had 'כל שיש בו', we might think rice and millet are left out only because they come in mixtures. Then we would think plain rice and millet DO get מזונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he had only taught us 'anything that has [grain] in it,' I would have said: anything with the five grains in it, yes, it gets מזונות. But rice and millet, no, because they are inside a mixture. However, when rice or millet is eaten plain, I would say that even rice and millet get the ברכה בורא מיני מזונות.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא explains why the first statement, 'כל שהוא', was also needed. It sets up the mistaken idea (הוה אמינא) that we would have had without it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that 'כל שיש בו' could be read as a rule only about mixtures. In that reading, rice and millet would be excluded only when they are mixed into something. That would leave room to think that plain rice or millet, eaten by itself, gets מזונות.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have said (a mistaken first assumption)
Rice and millet
A mixture
It is in its original, plain form (not mixed)
The ברכה 'Who creates kinds of nourishment' (the מזונות ברכה)

phrases.english: And if he had only taught us 'anything that has in it'

phrases.aramaic: הָוֵה אָמֵינָא כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ חֲמֵשֶׁת הַמִּינִים — אִין,
phrases.english: I would have said: anything that has the five grains in it, yes [it gets מזונות],
but rice and millet, no,
because they are [eaten] as part of a mixture.
phrases.notes: The mistaken reason: the mixture is what disqualifies them.

phrases.english: But when it is in its plain form,
I would say that even rice and millet as well
get the ברכה 'Who creates kinds of nourishment.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ הָוֵה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from explaining statement 2 to explaining why statement 1 was needed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Plain (unmixed) rice and millet might get בורא מיני מזונות, because they would be excluded only when mixed.

steps.title: Only the five grains get מזונות, even rice eaten plain does not
steps.stepSummary: 'כל שהוא מחמשת המינים' teaches that only the five grains get בורא מיני מזונות. Rice and millet are left out even when they are eaten plain.
steps.simpleTranslation: So he teaches us: it is anything that is one of the five grains that gets the ברכה 'Who creates kinds of nourishment.' This leaves out rice and millet: even when eaten plain, we do not say 'Who creates kinds of nourishment' over them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. The first statement teaches that מזונות belongs only to the five grains, so rice and millet never get it, even when eaten plain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'שהוא' (that IS one of the five grains) limits the ברכה to the five grains themselves. That shuts down the idea from Step 2. Rice and millet are not excluded because of mixing. They are excluded because they are not among the five grains. Now both statements of רב ושמואל have a job.

keyTerms.meaning: Anything that IS one of the five grains (wheat, barley, spelt, oats, rye)
To exclude

steps.whatToRemember: Two statements, two lessons. 'כל שיש בו' teaches that mixtures of the five grains get מזונות. 'כל שהוא' teaches that ONLY the five grains get מזונות, so rice and millet are excluded even when plain (at least at this point in the סוגיא).

phrases.english: So he teaches us:
anything that is one of the five grains,

phrases.aramaic: הוּא דִּמְבָרְכִין עָלָיו בּוֹרֵא מִינֵי מְזוֹנוֹת,
phrases.english: it is that which gets the ברכה 'Who creates kinds of nourishment,'
to exclude rice and millet,
which, even when they are in their plain form,
we do not say 'Who creates kinds of nourishment' over them.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן — כֹּל שֶׁהוּא מֵחֲמֵשֶׁת הַמִּינִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects the הוה אמינא of Step 2.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the five grains get בורא מיני מזונות; rice and millet are excluded even plain.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Each statement of רב ושמואל teaches something unique; rice and millet do not get מזונות.

steps.title: Challenge: a ברייתא says rice bread gets ברכות like a cooked grain dish
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 3 with a ברייתא: rice bread and millet bread get ברכות before and after 'כמעשה קדרה', like a cooked grain dish.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really not say 'Who creates kinds of nourishment' over rice and millet? But a ברייתא teaches: if they brought him rice bread or millet bread, he makes a ברכה over it before and after, like a cooked grain dish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the conclusion it just reached, that rice and millet never get מזונות. It quotes a ברייתא that seems to treat rice bread like a cooked grain dish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If rice bread gets ברכות 'like a מעשה קדרה', and a מעשה קדרה gets מזונות, then rice should get מזונות. The next step brings a second ברייתא to show that a מעשה קדרה does get מזונות, which completes the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Rice bread
Before and after (a ברכה before eating and one after)
A cooked dish (here: a cooked grain dish of the five grains)

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹרֶז וְדוֹחַן לָא מְבָרְכִינַן ״בּוֹרֵא מִינֵי מְזוֹנוֹת״?
phrases.english: And over rice and millet we do not say 'Who creates kinds of nourishment'?
phrases.notes: This sounds like a question, but the גמרא is really raising a challenge.

phrases.english: But it was taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: הֵבִיאוּ לְפָנָיו פַּת אוֹרֶז וּפַת דּוֹחַן —
phrases.english: If they brought before him rice bread or millet bread,
he makes a ברכה over it before and after
like a cooked grain dish.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוֹרֶז וְדוֹחַן לָא מְבָרְכִינַן בּוֹרֵא מִינֵי מְזוֹנוֹת? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of Step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that rice and millet do not get בורא מיני מזונות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא compares rice bread to a מעשה קדרה, which gets מזונות, so rice seems to get מזונות too.

steps.title: Completing the challenge: what ברכות a cooked grain dish gets
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא shows that a מעשה קדרה gets בורא מיני מזונות before and ברכה מעין שלש after. That seems to prove rice gets the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about a cooked grain dish, a ברייתא teaches: at the start he says 'Who creates kinds of nourishment,' and at the end he says the one ברכה that summarizes the three (ברכה מעין שלש).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes building its challenge. It shows from another ברייתא exactly which ברכות a מעשה קדרה gets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Put the two sources together. Rice bread is 'like a מעשה קדרה', and a מעשה קדרה gets מזונות before and מעין שלש after. So rice bread should get מזונות and מעין שלש. That directly contradicts Step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: And regarding
The one after-ברכה that summarizes the three ברכות of ברכת המזון (על המחיה)

phrases.english: And regarding a cooked grain dish it was taught:
At the start he says over it 'Who creates kinds of nourishment,'
and at the end he says over it
one ברכה that summarizes the three.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְגַבֵּי מַעֲשֵׂה קְדֵרָה תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the second piece needed to make the challenge of Step 4 work.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that rice and millet do not get בורא מיני מזונות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since a מעשה קדרה gets מזונות and מעין שלש, rice bread ('like a מעשה קדרה') should get them too.

steps.title: Answer: rice is like a cooked dish in one way, but not in another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that rice bread is like a מעשה קדרה only in getting a ברכה before AND after. Its actual ברכות are שהכל before and בורא נפשות after.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like a cooked dish and not like a cooked dish. It is like a cooked dish in that it gets a ברכה before and after. It is not like a cooked dish, because a cooked dish gets 'Who creates kinds of nourishment' at the start and the ברכה summarizing three at the end. Here, however, at the start one says 'by Whose word everything came to be' (שהכל), and at the end 'Who creates many living things and their needs, for all that You created' (בורא נפשות).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The comparison in the ברייתא is only partial: rice bread, like a cooked dish, needs a ברכה before and after, but the ברכות themselves are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'כמעשה קדרה' in the ברייתא refer only to the fact that there is a ברכה at both ends. They do not mean the same ברכות. Rice bread gets שהכל and בורא נפשות. So the ruling of Step 3, that rice does not get מזונות, survives.

keyTerms.meaning: Whereas here (contrasting two cases)
The general ברכה שהכל ('by Whose word everything came to be')
The short after-ברכה for most foods

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume 'like a מעשה קדרה' means 'gets the same ברכות as a מעשה קדרה.' The גמרא limits the comparison to having a ברכה before AND after.

phrases.english: Like a cooked dish, and not like a cooked dish:

phrases.aramaic: כְּמַעֲשֵׂה קְדֵרָה דִּמְבָרְכִין עָלָיו תְּחִלָּה וָסוֹף,
phrases.english: like a cooked dish in that one makes a ברכה over it before and after,
and not like a cooked dish,
because with a cooked dish,
at the start [one says] 'Who creates kinds of nourishment'
and at the end the ברכה summarizing three,
whereas here,
at the start one says over it 'by Whose word everything came to be,'
and at the end 'Who creates many living things and their needs,
for all that You have created.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַעֲשֵׂה קְדֵרָה וְלָא כְּמַעֲשֵׂה קְדֵרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Steps 4-5 by reading the ברייתא's comparison narrowly.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Like a מעשה קדרה' means rice bread gets the same ברכות: מזונות and מעין שלש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The comparison is only about having a ברכה before and after; rice bread gets שהכל and בורא נפשות.

steps.title: New challenge: a ברייתא lists rice as a cooked grain dish
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again with a ברייתא that lists אורז among the true מעשה קדרה dishes, next to forms of crushed wheat.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is rice not a cooked dish? But a ברייתא teaches: these are cooked dishes: wheat split in two, wheat crushed in three, fine flour, wheat crushed in four, wheat crushed in five, and rice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of Step 6, which treated rice as different from a real מעשה קדרה. It brings a ברייתא that lists rice right alongside wheat dishes as a מעשה קדרה. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If rice is a full מעשה קדרה like the wheat dishes, it should get the same ברכות, מזונות and מעין שלש. That would undo both Step 6 and Step 3. The next step answers this challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Wheat kernels split into two
Wheat kernels crushed into three
Fine flour
Wheat kernels crushed into four
Wheat kernels crushed into five

phrases.english: And is rice not a cooked dish?
phrases.notes: It sounds like a question, but it's really a challenge.

phrases.english: But it was taught: these are cooked dishes:
wheat split in two, wheat crushed in three, fine flour,
wheat crushed in four, wheat crushed in five, and rice.
phrases.notes: Rice is listed together with wheat dishes, which is the source of the challenge.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוֹרֶז לָאו מַעֲשֵׂה קְדֵרָה הוּא? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 6, which said rice differs from a real מעשה קדרה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that rice is only partly like a מעשה קדרה and does not get מזונות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא lists rice among genuine מעשה קדרה dishes, so it should get the full מעשה קדרה ברכות.

steps.title: The rice-as-cooked-dish ruling follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that treats rice as a real מעשה קדרה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי. He holds that rice is a true grain. The רבנן disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי יוחנן בן נורי. A ברייתא teaches that רבי יוחנן בן נורי says rice is a kind of grain. A person who eats it after it becomes חמץ is liable to כרת. A person can also fulfill his obligation of מצה with it on פסח. But the רבנן do not hold this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 7. The ברייתא that lists rice as a real מעשה קדרה follows only רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי treats rice as a true grain, so of course it can be a real grain dish. The רבנן do not treat rice as a grain. Step 3's rule (only the five grains get מזונות) follows the רבנן, so the challenge is removed.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this? (used to identify a source's author)
A type of grain
Its becoming leavened (חמץ)
Spiritual cutting off, the punishment for eating חמץ on פסח
Fulfilling one's obligation (here, eating מצה)

steps.confusionAlert: The proof about פסח (חמץ and מצה) is not a new topic. It shows how fully רבי יוחנן בן נורי treats rice as grain. If rice counts as grain for פסח, it also counts as grain for ברכות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a disagreement among תנאים about rice. The rest of the סוגיא depends on which side a source follows.

phrases.english: Whose opinion is this?
It is Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri says:
Rice is a type of grain,
and one is liable to karet for its leavened form,
phrases.notes: Eating rice חמץ on פסח would carry the full punishment.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָדָם יוֹצֵא בּוֹ יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בַּפֶּסַח.
phrases.english: and a person fulfills his obligation with it on Pesach.
phrases.notes: Rice מצה counts for the מצוה.

phrases.english: But the Rabbis, no.
phrases.notes: The רבנן do not treat rice as grain.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מַנִּי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 7 by assigning that ברייתא to a minority תנא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the contradicting source to a different תנא (מאן תנא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא listing rice as מעשה קדרה seemed to be the accepted view and to contradict Step 3.
steps.terutzMaskana: That ברייתא follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי. The רבנן, whose view Step 3 follows, do not treat rice as grain.

steps.title: Challenge: do the רבנן really disagree? A תוספתא on wheat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the רבנן really disagree. It begins quoting a תוספתא, starting with the rules for wheat in different forms.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do the רבנן really not hold this? But a תוספתא teaches: someone who chews raw wheat says בורא פרי האדמה. If he ground it, baked it, and then cooked it, it depends. When the pieces stay whole, he says המוציא before and the three ברכות of ברכת המזון after. When the pieces do not stay whole, he says בורא מיני מזונות before and one ברכה מעין שלש after.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in Step 8. It starts quoting a תוספתא, and this wheat section sets up the comparison that comes next for rice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wheat section gives a baseline. Whole wheat bread gets המוציא and ברכת המזון, while dissolved bread gets מזונות and מעין שלש. Next the תוספתא gives the rice case, which is where the real challenge lies.

keyTerms.meaning: One who chews (raw kernels)
He ground it, baked it, and cooked it
The pieces (of bread) remain intact
The three ברכות of ברכת המזון
One ברכה that summarizes the three (על המחיה)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop here thinking this is the whole challenge. Wheat is just the baseline. The real challenge comes in the rice section of the same תוספתא.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis do not?!
But was it not taught:
One who chews wheat
recites over it 'Who creates fruit of the ground.'
If he ground it, baked it, and cooked it,
when the pieces are intact,

phrases.aramaic: בַּתְּחִלָּה מְבָרֵךְ עָלֶיהָ ״הַמּוֹצִיא לֶחֶם מִן הָאָרֶץ״,
phrases.english: at the start he recites 'Who brings forth bread from the earth,'
and at the end he recites three blessings.
If the pieces are not intact,
at the start he recites 'Who creates kinds of nourishment,'

phrases.aramaic: וּלְבַסּוֹף מְבָרֵךְ עָלֶיהָ בְּרָכָה אַחַת מֵעֵין שָׁלֹשׁ.
phrases.english: and at the end he recites one blessing abridged from the three.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן לָא וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 8's claim that the רבנן do not treat rice as a grain dish.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 8's claim that the רבנן reject rice as a grain (מזונות) food.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A תוספתא, whose rice section follows, seems to give rice מזונות even according to the רבנן.

steps.title: The תוספתא's rice section: rice bread gets מזונות even when whole
steps.stepSummary: Raw rice gets בורא פרי האדמה. Rice that was ground, baked, and cooked gets בורא מיני מזונות and a ברכה מעין שלש, even when the pieces are intact.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who chews raw rice says בורא פרי האדמה. If he ground it, baked it, and cooked it, he says בורא מיני מזונות before and one ברכה מעין שלש after. This is true even when the pieces stay whole.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the heart of the challenge. The תוספתא says rice products get מזונות and מעין שלש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Compare this to wheat. Whole wheat pieces got המוציא, but whole rice pieces only get מזונות. So rice is treated as a grain food, but below the level of real bread. That contradicts Step 6, which gave rice bread only שהכל and בורא נפשות.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though
Rice

phrases.english: One who chews rice
recites over it 'Who creates fruit of the ground.'
If he ground it, baked it, and cooked it,
even though the pieces are intact,
phrases.notes: This is the key difference from wheat: no המוציא even when whole.

phrases.english: at the start he recites 'Who creates kinds of nourishment,'

phrases.aramaic: וּלְבַסּוֹף מְבָרֵךְ עָלָיו בְּרָכָה אַחַת מֵעֵין שָׁלֹשׁ.
phrases.english: and at the end he recites one blessing abridged from the three.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכּוֹסֵס אֶת הָאוֹרֶז מְבָרֵךְ עָלָיו בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הָאֲדָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the תוספתא begun in Step 9 and gives the actual evidence for the challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That someone (seemingly the רבנן) gives rice products בורא מיני מזונות and מעין שלש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rice section of the תוספתא, contrasted with its wheat section.

steps.title: This תוספתא cannot follow רבי יוחנן בן נורי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view the תוספתא follows. It cannot be רבי יוחנן בן נורי, because by his view whole rice bread would need המוציא and ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If you say it is רבי יוחנן בן נורי, who said rice is a kind of grain, then he should need to say המוציא and the three ברכות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules out רבי יוחנן בן נורי as the author of the תוספתא. This sets up the next move: the author must be the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן בן נורי, rice is a full grain, so whole rice bread should be treated exactly like wheat bread. The תוספתא only gives מזונות, so it must follow the רבנן. That would mean the רבנן also give rice מזונות, which contradicts Step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introducing an option that will be rejected)
He would need to recite

steps.whatToRemember: By process of elimination, the תוספתא seems to follow the רבנן. That would mean even the רבנן give rice בורא מיני מזונות, and the next step must deal with this.

phrases.english: Whose view is this?

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי הִיא
phrases.english: If you say it is Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri,
who said rice is a type of grain,
then 'Who brings forth bread from the earth'
and three blessings he would need to recite!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי אִילֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the תוספתא from Steps 9-10 to find its author and so sharpen the challenge against Step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא is the author of the תוספתא about rice?
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 8's claim that only רבי יוחנן בן נורי treats rice as a grain dish.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תוספתא cannot follow רבי יוחנן בן נורי, who would require המוציא. So it must follow the רבנן, which would mean the רבנן give rice מזונות.

steps.title: The תוספתא must follow the רבנן, refuting רב ושמואל
steps.stepSummary: The תוספתא cannot follow רבי יוחנן בן נורי, so it must follow the רבנן. That means rice gets בורא מיני מזונות even though it is not a true grain, which goes against רב ושמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it the view of the רבנן? Then this is a strong refutation of רב ושמואל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the question from Step 11. The תוספתא must follow the רבנן, and that clashes with רב ושמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ושמואל held that only the five grains get בורא מיני מזונות, so rice would not. The רבנן say rice is not a true grain, yet the תוספתא still gives cooked rice בורא מיני מזונות. So a תנאי source rules against רב ושמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it...? (a pushed conclusion)
A decisive refutation, usually from a תנאי source

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it the view of the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן בן נורי was ruled out in Step 11, so only the רבנן remain.

phrases.english: And then it is a refutation of Rav and Shmuel!
phrases.notes: רב ושמואל limited מזונות to the five grains.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו, רַבָּנַן הִיא, וּתְיוּבְתָּא דְּרַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the question of Step 11 by deciding who the author is and drawing the result.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ושמואל's rule that only the five grains get בורא מיני מזונות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תוספתא follows the רבנן, who do not treat rice as a grain, yet it still gives cooked rice מזונות. So the מזונות ברכה is not limited to the five grains.

steps.title: The refutation stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that רב ושמואל are refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits there is no answer. רב ושמואל's view is refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Repeating the single word תיובתא means the challenge is accepted. The conclusion is that cooked rice gets בורא מיני מזונות, even by the רבנן.
steps.whatToRemember: Cooked rice dishes get בורא מיני מזונות even though rice is not one of the five grains. רב ושמואל's narrower view was refuted.
steps.confusionAlert: Rice getting בורא מיני מזונות does not make it equal to the five grains. The תוספתא showed that even whole pieces of rice bread get only מזונות, never המוציא. The ברכה said after eating rice is a separate question, which the גמרא takes up in Steps 19–21.

phrases.english: It is a refutation.
phrases.notes: The challenge stands; there's no answer to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּיוּבְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the refutation raised in Step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב ושמואל are refuted. A cooked rice dish gets בורא מיני מזונות.

steps.title: Quoting the תוספתא's ruling on chewing raw wheat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the תוספתא and quotes its first line: someone who chews raw wheat says בורא פרי האדמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: One who chews wheat says בורא פרי האדמה over it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new discussion by quoting a line from the תוספתא again. It is setting up a question on this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Raw wheat kernels are not food made from grain, like bread or a cooked dish. So the תוספתא treats them like any produce of the ground. The next step will challenge which ברכה is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: One who chews raw kernels
Wheat

phrases.english: The Master said: One who chews wheat
phrases.notes: Re-quoting the תוספתא from Step 9.

phrases.english: says over it, "Who creates fruit of the ground."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: הַכּוֹסֵס אֶת הַחִטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After closing the rice and רב ושמואל discussion, the גמרא goes back to examine the details of the תוספתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Chewing raw wheat gets בורא פרי האדמה.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the blessing is 'Who creates kinds of seeds'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says chewed wheat gets בורא מיני זרעים, which contradicts the תוספתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: 'בורא מיני זרעים'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the תוספתא with a ברייתא that gives a different ברכה for chewed wheat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תוספתא gives the general ברכה for produce, בורא פרי האדמה. The ברייתא gives a more specific ברכה just for seeds. Both are תנאי sources, so they seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: "Who creates kinds of seeds," a specific ברכה for seeds

phrases.english: But it was taught: "Who creates kinds of seeds"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא בּוֹרֵא מִינֵי זְרָעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the line just quoted in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תוספתא's ruling that chewed wheat gets בורא פרי האדמה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two תנאי sources give different ברכות for the same food.

steps.title: Two different תנאים: רבי יהודה and the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The two sources follow different תנאים. The ברייתא with the specific ברכה follows רבי יהודה, and the תוספתא follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one is רבי יהודה, and this one is the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two sources do not contradict each other. Each one follows a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה gives a separate, specific ברכה for each kind of plant, so he says בורא מיני זרעים. The רבנן use one general ברכה, בורא פרי האדמה, for everything that grows from the ground.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces an answer)
This one... and that one... (assigns each source to a different view)

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This one is Rabbi Yehuda, and this one is the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: "Kinds of seeds" follows רבי יהודה. "Fruit of the ground" follows the רבנן.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וְהָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the two sources to different תנאים (a מחלוקת)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources state one agreed rule, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each source follows a different תנא. The רבנן give the general ברכה, and רבי יהודה gives the specific one.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה: רבי יהודה requires specific blessings
steps.stepSummary: The משנה shows the same מחלוקת with vegetables. The רבנן say בורא פרי האדמה, and רבי יהודה says בורא מיני דשאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in the משנה: Over vegetables one says בורא פרי האדמה. רבי יהודה says: בורא מיני דשאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves its answer from our משנה. There, רבי יהודה also requires a specific ברכה where the רבנן give the general one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For vegetables, רבי יהודה wants a specific ברכה for that group. So it makes sense that for seeds he would also want a specific ברכה, בורא מיני זרעים. This supports linking the ברייתא to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Vegetables
"Who creates kinds of herbs," רבי יהודה's ברכה for vegetables

steps.whyThisMatters: The practical ruling follows the רבנן. Anything that grows from the ground and is not a grain product, a tree fruit, or a special food gets the general ברכה of בורא פרי האדמה.

phrases.english: As we learned in the Mishnah:
And over vegetables one says, "Who creates fruit of the ground."
phrases.notes: This is the view of the רבנן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: "Who creates kinds of herbs."

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: וְעַל יְרָקוֹת אוֹמֵר בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הָאֲדָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source that backs up the answer in Step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה requires specific ברכות while the רבנן use the general בורא פרי האדמה
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה, the מחלוקת about vegetables

steps.title: Quoting the תוספתא's ruling on rice again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the rice line of the תוספתא again. Raw rice gets בורא פרי האדמה. Ground, baked, and cooked rice gets בורא מיני מזונות before and a ברכה מעין שלש after, even if the pieces are whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: One who chews rice says בורא פרי האדמה over it. If he ground it, baked it, and cooked it, even though the pieces are whole, at the start he says בורא מיני מזונות, and at the end one ברכה מעין שלש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the rice line again to analyze its details. It is setting up a question that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier this text was used to identify the author. Now the גמרא repeats it to examine the ruling itself. The final clause, a ברכה מעין שלש after rice, is unusual because rice is not one of the five grains, so it is likely the target of the coming question.

keyTerms.meaning: Rice
He ground it, baked it, and cooked it
The pieces are still whole
One ברכה that sums up the three ברכות of ברכת המזון

phrases.english: The Master said: One who chews rice
phrases.notes: The same תוספתא quoted in Step 10, repeated here for a new discussion.

phrases.english: says over it, "Who creates fruit of the ground."
If he ground it, baked it, and cooked it,
even though the pieces are whole,
phrases.notes: With the five grains, whole pieces would mean the food counts as bread.

phrases.english: at the start he says over it, "Who creates kinds of nourishment,"
and at the end, one blessing that sums up the three.
phrases.notes: This clause is what the גמרא will question next.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר, הַכּוֹסֵס אֶת הָאוֹרֶז מְבָרֵךְ עָלָיו בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הָאֲדָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the wheat line, the גמרא moves on to the next line of the same תוספתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Raw rice gets בורא פרי האדמה. Processed rice gets בורא מיני מזונות before and a ברכה מעין שלש after, even when the pieces are whole.

steps.title: A ברייתא says rice gets nothing special at the end
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ruling that cooked rice gets a ברכה מעין שלש afterward. A ברייתא says no such ברכה is said.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא: at the end, nothing at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last part of the תוספתא from Step 18. That part said cooked rice gets a ברכה מעין שלש after eating, and a ברייתא says it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Nothing at all" does not mean no ברכה whatsoever. It means none of the special ברכות, such as מעין שלש, so the person just says the general בורא נפשות. The two sources now directly contradict each other about rice.

keyTerms.meaning: At the end, meaning the ברכה said after eating
And nothing at all, meaning no special ברכה

steps.confusionAlert: "ולא כלום" does not mean you eat rice with no ברכה afterward. It means you do not say מעין שלש. You still say the basic בורא נפשות.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: at the end, nothing at all!
phrases.notes: Meaning no מעין שלש, only בורא נפשות.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברכה אחרונה for rice stated in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תוספתא's ruling that cooked rice requires a ברכה מעין שלש afterward.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא of equal authority says rice requires no special ברכה at the end, which is a direct contradiction.

steps.title: רב ששת: the two sources follow different opinions
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the תוספתא follows רבן גמליאל and the ברייתא follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: This is not difficult. This source follows רבן גמליאל, and that source follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת resolves the contradiction by saying each source follows a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source requiring מעין שלש for rice follows רבן גמליאל. The source requiring nothing special follows the רבנן. This only makes sense if רבן גמליאל is generally one level stricter than the רבנן, and the next step proves that.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; this opens an answer
This one... and that one; assigns each source to a different view

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: It is not difficult:
This one is Rabban Gamliel, and that one is the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: מעין שלש for rice follows רבן גמליאל. "Nothing" follows the רבנן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the sources to different תנאים (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to give one agreed-upon ruling about rice, so they contradicted each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sources reflect a real dispute. רבן גמליאל requires מעין שלש for rice, and the רבנן require only בורא נפשות.

steps.title: Proof: רבן גמליאל is one level stricter on the seven species
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that for the שבעת המינים, רבן גמליאל requires all three ברכות and the חכמים require one ברכה מעין שלש.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: This is the rule. Anything from the seven species: רבן גמליאל says three ברכות, and the חכמים say one ברכה that summarizes the three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to prove that רבן גמליאל and the רבנן really disagree about the ברכה אחרונה, with רבן גמליאל always one level higher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the שבעת המינים, רבן גמליאל requires full ברכת המזון and the חכמים require מעין שלש. Moving one step down to rice, רבן גמליאל requires מעין שלש and the חכמים require nothing special. This pattern is what supports רב ששת's assignment.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule
The seven species for which ארץ ישראל is praised
The three main ברכות of ברכת המזון
One ברכה that summarizes the three (for example, על המחיה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute is the source of our practice. We follow the חכמים and say מעין שלש after the שבעת המינים.

phrases.english: As it was taught: This is the rule:
Anything that is from the seven species,
Rabban Gamliel says three blessings,

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים בְּרָכָה אַחַת מֵעֵין שָׁלֹשׁ.
phrases.english: and the Sages say one blessing abridged from the three.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, זֶה הַכְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב ששת's answer in Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That רבן גמליאל and the רבנן disagree about the ברכה אחרונה, with רבן גמליאל one level stricter.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the שבעת המינים.

steps.title: The story in יריחו: רבי עקיבא says the short ברכה
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל and the זקנים ate dates in יריחו. When רבן גמליאל let רבי עקיבא lead the ברכה, he quickly said only מעין שלש.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a story: רבן גמליאל and the elders were reclining in an upper room in יריחו. Dates were brought before them and they ate. רבן גמליאל gave רבי עקיבא permission to lead the ברכה. רבי עקיבא jumped in and said one ברכה מעין שלש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows the dispute from Step 21 being lived out in practice. This step sets up the exchange that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dates are one of the שבעת המינים. רבי עקיבא followed the חכמים and said only מעין שלש, even though רבן גמליאל, the נשיא who was present, holds that three ברכות are required.

keyTerms.meaning: A story or incident
Reclining, meaning seated together for a meal
Dates (a stage of ripening); one of the seven species
Permission (here, to lead the ברכה)
He jumped, meaning he acted quickly

phrases.english: And there was an incident with Rabban Gamliel and the elders
who were reclining in an upper room in Jericho,
and they brought dates before them and they ate,

phrases.aramaic: וְנָתַן רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל רְשׁוּת לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְבָרֵךְ.
phrases.english: and Rabban Gamliel gave Rabbi Akiva permission to bless.
Rabbi Akiva jumped in and blessed
one blessing abridged from the three.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְהַזְּקֵנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from Step 21 with a story that illustrates the dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא said only מעין שלש over dates, following the חכמים.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל rebukes רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל objects that רבי עקיבא keeps getting involved in disputes against him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said to him: עקיבא, how long will you stick your head into the dispute!
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל challenges רבי עקיבא for following the opposing view in front of him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The complaint is that רבי עקיבא acted on a disputed position, against the view of רבן גמליאל, the נשיא. This sets up רבי עקיבא's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Until when; how long
Putting your head in, meaning getting involved
A dispute

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel said to him: Akiva,

phrases.aramaic: עַד מָתַי אַתָּה מַכְנִיס רֹאשְׁךָ בֵּין הַמַּחֲלוֹקֶת!
phrases.english: until when will you stick your head into the dispute!

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲקִיבָא, עַד מָתַי אַתָּה מַכְנִיס רֹאשְׁךָ בֵּין הַמַּחֲלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to רבי עקיבא's action in Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's choice to say only מעין שלש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He acted on one side of a dispute, against the view of רבן גמליאל, the נשיא.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the הלכה follows the majority
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers that רבן גמליאל himself taught that the הלכה follows the many against an individual.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Our teacher, even though you say this and your colleagues say that, you taught us, our teacher: when an individual disagrees with the many, the הלכה follows the many.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא defends himself by using a rule that רבן גמליאל himself taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל is a single opinion against the חכמים. By the rule of יחיד ורבים הלכה כרבים, the הלכה is מעין שלש, even against the נשיא.

keyTerms.meaning: Our teacher
Your colleagues (the חכמים)
When one disagrees with many, the halacha follows the many

steps.whatToRemember: For the שבעת המינים, the הלכה follows the חכמים: one ברכה מעין שלש afterward, not the full ברכת המזון.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the general rule of following the majority applies even against the נשיא.

phrases.english: He said to him: Our teacher,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאַתָּה אוֹמֵר כֵּן
phrases.english: even though you say this
and your colleagues say that,
you taught us, our teacher:
an individual and the many, the halacha follows the many.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: רַבֵּינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבן גמליאל's rebuke in Step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Following the view of the חכמים against the נשיא seemed improper.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים are the majority, so the halacha follows them.

steps.title: רבי יהודה begins another version of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה begins quoting a different version of the dispute about the seven species.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says in his name: Anything that is from the seven species
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new version of the dispute, quoted by רבי יהודה in someone's name. This step sets up a statement that continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רש״י, "his name" refers to רבן גמליאל: רבי יהודה reports רבן גמליאל's view in a different version. The full content of this version comes in the next section, so here we only have the opening words.

keyTerms.meaning: In his name

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says in his name:
phrases.notes: According to רש״י, in the name of רבן גמליאל.

phrases.english: anything that is from the seven species
phrases.notes: Continues on the next amud.
